_about: Hue arcs for the Sharket theme. This is the INPUT the theme is derived from: sharket_theme.json is generated by running the role ramp over each accent below. Regenerate rather than hand-editing the output.
_emission: Every category emits the FULL rung ladder, not only the tiers a coverage snapshot lists. A missing tier row inside an existing category does not fall back to Default: ttheme is {} and parse_rgba(None) returns white, so the block renders white text + white border on black. A tier key nobody asks for is never read, so a superset is free and the tree can move between exports without breaking a block.

_rules.band: A family owns a hue band. Bands must not overlap and must sit at least 6 degrees apart. Inside a band, closeness is deliberate: you should read 'currency' before 'which currency'.
_rules.text: Authored text is walked along its own hue until it clears 4.5:1 on its plate. Rarity-inherited labels cannot be recoloured, so the plate yields instead, to the 3:1 large-text floor.
_rules.border: Borders are graphical marks: 3:1 floor. PoE has no border width, so colour is the whole budget. Border means STATE, never rank.
_rules.rarity_inherited: Families that emit no TextColor cap plates at L<=7 (set by magic blue) and never drop the plate: with no text colour, a plateless row does nothing but shrink the label below the game's own 32.

notes.Gold: auto-picked, so capped at FontSize 35 — it only ever needs acknowledging

notes.Oils: chartreuse, held 8 degrees clear of the warm band so a Golden Oil never reads as a Divine. Minimap icon shape = Circle (Sharket's trick: shape identifies the mechanic, colour and size carry the tier).

notes.Enshrouding Crystals: inherits the incubator accent — it is the 3.29 incubator replacement, so muscle memory carries over

notes.Fragment Splinters: also emitted as 'Splinters'. Moved INTO the maps band — it was gold, which read as currency.
notes.Scarabs: Maps/Scarabs.json still shares 'Map Fragments' in the tree; this key is waiting for the retag. Inside the band on purpose: 'atlas consumable' should read before 'which one'.

notes.Curse of the Allflame: covers the league's own basetypes: ducats, voyage maps, wish bottles. Member of this family rather than its own — you should read 'league drop' before 'which league'.
notes.Stackable Currency: shared fallback still used by League Items.json, Enshrouding Crystals.json and Incursion Vials.json. League content, so it sits here rather than in the warm band — at 52 degrees it was 2 degrees from Default, i.e. 'league currency' and 'unmapped junk' were the same colour.

notes.Heist: also emitted as Heist Currency / Heist Contracts / Heist Blueprints / Heist Equipment / Heist Targets. Blueprints outrank contracts by tier NUMBER, since they share one accent.

hue_exempt._why: Saturation <= 30 with no TextColor emitted, so hue carries almost nothing — rarity, size and border do the work. Exempt from the band rule by construction.

notes.Influenced: The state treatment expressed as category rows: gear, so no TextColor and plates capped at L<=7, with influence purple 150 0 255 forced onto the border at T0-T4. When influence becomes a rule-level state, this key stops being read and can be deleted with no visual change.
notes.Magic Net: A suppression ladder, not a value ladder — T4 keeps good jewellery alive, T5 kills the rest — so it is capped at FontSize 35 and never competes.

authored._why: Two families cannot come from the generic ramp.

Tainted Currency._why: Grey means corruption: it gives up its hue on the PLATE so a tainted orb can never be read as its clean counterpart.

Exotic bases._why: Tier 5 is their ONLY visible tier, so it must not inherit the gear 'bulk' no-plate/FS30 row — that sits below the game's own default of 32.

Heist Experimented._why: Three tiers, none of them a chase — every experimented base is just 'notable, worth a look', so it caps at 40.

states._about: Rule-level, NOT part of theme_category x Tier N. Most rules get no state hue. Escalation: enhanced = plate steps down within the family's cap and the state hue takes the border; swap = the state hue becomes a bright plate and the accent drops to the border. Font size never changes: a state says what an item is, not what it's worth.

enshrouded_allflame.note: unique-only; it is the existing 'Enshrouded (Vestigial)' Tier 2 rule

influenced.note: swap if you want it unmistakable

states.fractured_note: Equipment/Special/Fractured.json still declares theme_category 'Body Armours', so a fractured bow renders as body armour — this is the last of the three equipment-state collisions.

enchanted.note: also the heist blueprint/contract enchant bias

replica.note: 49 degrees from foulborn so the siblings never blur

reserved._why: The apex is FULL: Tier 0 owns the near-white plate and Tier 1 the brightest accent plate, both at FontSize 45, so a rung above them could only duplicate one of the two. 'Base + influence' is therefore the swap treatment, not a new tier. Headroom exists only at the quiet end.
reserved._emitted: T8 and T12 are emitted with every accent-text category, so inserting a quiet tier renders correctly instead of white-on-black. They are QUIETER than hide: an unauthored tier above the authored range clamps to the quietest authored rung, never the numerically nearest one.
reserved._absent_for_rarity_inherited: Deliberately NOT emitted for gear, Campaign, Influenced, Magic Net and the exotic bases. With no TextColor and plates capped at L<=7, T6/T7/T9 already exhaust the quiet end, so T8/T12 could only duplicate them byte-for-byte. A gear category that needs another quiet rung should reuse T7.
